disease_label_per_paper: Fulminant hepatitis A complicated by Takotsubo syndrome treated with plasma exchange
presentation_summary: Healthy 61-year-old woman presented after one week of asthenia and nausea with acute liver failure labs at another institution: AST 12760 U/L, ALT 11864 U/L, bilirubin 5.3 mg/dL, and INR 3.5.

At liver ICU admission she was hemodynamically stable with jaundice and no hepatic encephalopathy; labs showed AST 5206 U/L, ALT 7829 U/L, GGT 256 U/L, ALP 164 U/L, total bilirubin 6.9 mg/dL, INR 3.9, and ammonia 86 umol/L.
Abdominal ultrasound was normal; initial ECG and echocardiogram were essentially normal, and biopsy plus serology supported severe acute hepatitis A context.

On ICU day 2 she developed grade IV hepatic encephalopathy requiring intubation, bilirubin 14.1 mg/dL, INR 2.7, ammonia 132 umol/L, TCD evidence of intracranial hypertension, troponin I 11.19 ng/mL, ejection fraction 32%, and hypotension requiring dobutamine and norepinephrine.

Liver transplant was contraindicated by cardiogenic shock with severe cardiac dysfunction; three sessions of standard-volume plasma exchange were followed by neurologic, liver-test, ammonia, INR, TCD, and cardiac-function improvement; she was extubated on day 9 and discharged to the ward on day 14.
